title: CSS Flexbox
subtitle: Build flexible one-dimensional layouts with Flexbox.
description: Learn how to align, distribute and organize elements efficiently using containers, rows, columns and flexible sizing.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 6: CSS Flexbox. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “CSS Flexbox”. The goal is to build flexible one-dimensional layouts with Flexbox.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
Flexbox is designed for arranging items along one main axis. The container controls direction and alignment, while flex items can grow or shrink based on available space.

options: CSS Grid is the only layout that can align items.

blocks.question: A row uses justify-content but the items align on the wrong direction after flex-direction changes. Why?
options: The main and cross axes depend on flex-direction.

blocks.explanation: Flexbox axes change with direction, so alignment properties must be interpreted against those axes.

blocks.question: A program repeatedly looks up a learner by a unique email address. Which structure is a natural fit?
options: A map/dictionary keyed by email, with suitable uniqueness handling.
A random number with no mapping.
A paragraph of comma-separated values that is never parsed.
A loop that guesses the correct person.
blocks.explanation: Key-value structures express lookup by identifier more directly than repeatedly scanning unrelated data.
